_comment: Questions for the pre-rendered Q&A pages at /answers/. ANSWERS ARE QUOTED, NEVER GENERATED. Each citation names a filing, a page, and a verbatim passage; scripts/verify-citations.mjs proves at build time that the passage appears on that page. `framing` is the single human-authored sentence per question, so a human owns every word on the page that is not a quotation from the record.
_scope_rule: Court-record questions only. Questions that invite a characterisation of a third party are out of scope by construction and are not listed here. The question set is seeded from the court-record subset of the existing /faq/ and /is-conrad-rockenhaus-dead/ pages, and is designed to be swapped for real Google Search Console query data when that arrives: add or replace entries here and the pages regenerate.

questions.question: When is the next motion hearing in Wayne County divorce case 26-104594-DO?
questions.framing: The hearing date, time, and judge are stated in the Consolidated Notice of Hearing filed July 2, 2026.

citations.quote: will be brought on for hearing before the Honorable Nicole N. Goodson, Third Judicial Circuit Court for the County of Wayne, Family Division, on August 26, 2026 at 11:30 a.m., or as soon thereafter as the parties may be heard

questions.question: What motions are scheduled for hearing on August 26, 2026 in case 26-104594-DO?
questions.framing: The Consolidated Notice of Hearing lists ten motions set for the same date.

citations.quote: PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that the following ten (10) motions of Defendant/Counter-Plaintiff Conrad Alan Rockenhaus will be brought on for hearing
Omnibus Motion (Preservation of Evidence; Financial Disclosure; rockenhaus.com Domain Temporary Restraining Order)

questions.question: What does the motion to appoint a guardian ad litem ask the court to do?
questions.framing: The relief requested is set out in the motion filed July 2, 2026 under MCR 2.201(E).

citations.quote: Appointing a guardian ad litem for Plaintiff, or a next friend as the Court deems appropriate to Plaintiff's posture, pursuant to MCR 2.201(E), if the Court determines that Plaintiff lacks the capacity to represent her own interests
Deferring entry of any default judgment or other dispositive relief against Plaintiff until Plaintiff is represented by a duly appointed guardian ad litem, next friend, or counsel

questions.question: Does appointing a guardian ad litem decide anything about the merits of the case?
questions.framing: The motion states expressly what an appointment does and does not determine.

citations.quote: Appointment does not resolve, and is not a finding upon, the merits of any claim or defense, or the liability of the person for whom a representative is appointed. It ensures only that the person is represented while the merits are decided.

questions.question: What Michigan court rule governs appointing a guardian ad litem in a civil case?
questions.framing: The motion cites the rule and states the standard it applies.

citations.quote: MCR 2.201(E) governs the representation of incompetent persons in civil proceedings. Where an incompetent person who is subject to the jurisdiction of the court does not have a conservator or other legal representative, the court is to appoint a guardian ad litem or next friend to protect that person's interests

questions.question: Did the plaintiff file an answer to the counterclaim for divorce in case 26-104594-DO?
questions.framing: An Answer to Part III, Counterclaim for Divorce was filed on the plaintiff's behalf by counsel; the filing is in the record as a scanned document.
questions.record_gap: This filing is a scanned image with no text layer. A machine transcription makes it searchable, but that transcription is not reliable enough to quote, so it is cited by document and page rather than reproduced.

references.note: Caption page of the Answer to Part III, Counterclaim for Divorce, filed on the plaintiff's behalf by counsel of record.
Related opposing filing: Motion to Set Aside Default of Counterclaim.

_answer_support_note: A question is supported by `citations` (verbatim, verified against a native-text page) or by `references` (the filing and page, named and linked, without reproducing its words). References exist because 77 pages of this record are readable only via machine transcription: OCR makes those filings findable and describable, but it interleaves margin text into body lines, so quoting it would put words in a court document that the document does not contain. scripts/verify-citations.mjs refuses a quoted citation to an OCR page, and the schema refuses a question with neither citations nor references.
